title: Forward Deployed Engineering 101 — Kevin Bai, Anthropic, ex Palantir & Rippling Founding FDE
talk_summary: Kevin Bai explains Palantir's Forward Deployed Engineer model: engineers who build custom solutions for non-technical enterprise buyers, but only on top of a shared platform of primitives so work isn't rebuilt from scratch. He argues AI has made every platform customizable, so more companies will face the 'technical product, non-technical buyer' gap that FDEs fill.

takeaways.technique: Shared primitives layer instead of bespoke per-project builds
takeaways.what_they_do: FDEs never write software from scratch; they assemble solutions from a common set of platform primitives, and anything generalizable gets promoted back into the platform.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They are never writing software from scratch. Right? There is already a set of primitives on top of which they could assemble them

takeaways.what_they_do: Anything bespoke and unique to one customer stays local; anything generalizable is generalized into the platform long term.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Anything that's bespoke and unique to a particular customer um is uh something that should really only exist for that one customer. Anything that can be generalizable should be generalized

takeaways.technique: No single point of failure on a workstream
takeaways.what_they_do: Encourages multiple engineers on a project so knowledge isn't held by one person who can vanish.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the last thing you want is like a single point of failure, right? Where uh one person knows all the information, they go on vacation

takeaways.what_they_do: Advises checking whether the specific corner case exists before standing up an FDE function, rather than adopting it because it's in vogue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do I need an FTE function? Like, do I need one? Not want, right?
